name: mwifiex_parse_tdls_event
prose: Handles a TDLS generic event from the mwifiex firmware (real name mwifiex_parse_tdls_event(priv, event_skb), sta_event.c:245-334; static, returns int). It reads the event structure just after the event-cause word in event_skb->data. It returns -1 (logging) if event_skb->len is shorter than sizeof(struct mwifiex_tdls_generic_event) - sizeof(u16) - sizeof(adapter->event_cause), and -1 if mwifiex_get_sta_entry finds no station for the peer MAC. Otherwise it switches on the event type: TDLS_EVENT_LINK_TEAR_DOWN calls cfg80211_tdls_oper_request(NL80211_TDLS_TEARDOWN) with the event's reason code (tdls_status is not changed); TDLS_EVENT_CHAN_SWITCH_RESULT logs the result and, if switch_result.status is non-zero, sets tdls_status to TDLS_IN_BASE_CHAN or TDLS_IN_OFF_CHAN according to cur_chan (unchanged for other values) and returns 0; on a successful switch, for TDLS_BASE_CHANNEL it calls mwifiex_update_ralist_tx_pause_in_tdls_cs(priv, mac, false) and sets TDLS_IN_BASE_CHAN, and for TDLS_OFF_CHANNEL it calls it with true and sets TDLS_IN_OFF_CHAN, each only when the status is not already that value; TDLS_EVENT_START_CHAN_SWITCH sets tdls_status to TDLS_CHAN_SWITCHING; TDLS_EVENT_CHAN_SWITCH_STOPPED only logs the reason; an unknown type does nothing. All of these paths return 0. It keeps no lock or reference on the station entry.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function mwifiex_parse_tdls_event (the listed name mwifiex_process_tdls_event does not exist); old prose said 'on every one of these paths returns 0' next to the -1 paths, now separated

name: mwifiex_process_uap_event
prose: Handles a firmware event for an AP-mode mwifiex interface (real name mwifiex_process_uap_event(priv), uap_event.c:94-347; the slice shows only its tail; returns int). It switches on adapter->event_cause. EVENT_UAP_STA_ASSOC allocates a station_info (-ENOMEM if that fails), parses the association event, validates the management frame/length (returning -1 on malformed input) and reports the new station to cfg80211; STA_DEAUTH, BSS_IDLE/ACTIVE/START, MIC countermeasures, AMSDU aggregation control, ADDBA/DELBA/BA-stream timeout and TX status report update state or call helpers; EXT_SCAN_REPORT returns mwifiex_handle_event_ext_scan_report's result directly; PS_SLEEP and PS_AWAKE update adapter->ps_state and the pm_wakeup/tx_lock flags, and PS_AWAKE can return 0 early after sending a last-indication null packet; CHANNEL_REPORT_RDY, RADAR_DETECTED, BT_COEX_WLAN_PARA_CHANGE, TX_DATA_PAUSE, MULTI_CHAN_INFO and RXBA_SYNC call their handlers; REMAIN_ON_CHAN_EXPIRED reports expiry to cfg80211 and zeroes priv->roc_cfg; an unknown event id only logs. It returns 0 unless one of the explicit error returns (-ENOMEM, -1) or the ext-scan handler's result applies.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; the slice is the tail of mwifiex_process_uap_event (uap_event.c:94-347); the old prose said it returns 0 on every path, but 94-110 return -ENOMEM and several -1 returns exist; partly read: first 40 lines and tail, the middle only as case labels and return statements

name: mwifiex_usb_aggr_tx_data
prose: Decides whether to aggregate, send or defer a TX data packet on a mwifiex USB data port (usb.c:951-1121; static; the slice cut the head; the caller must not free skb afterwards, it is either queued, attached to a URB context, or, on some failure paths, completed). It computes the alignment padding and sets decision flags: if tx_param says another packet is queued it either flushes the pending aggregate and postcopies the current packet (when it would exceed the maximum size), or precopies the current packet and flushes the aggregate if the next packet would not fit (size or packet-count limits); if it is the last packet it precopies it and flushes the aggregate if packets are pending (sending the current packet separately first if it does not fit), otherwise sends it immediately. A null power-management packet is redirected to be sent separately (flushing the aggregate first when it is non-empty). Precopy: the skb is appended to port->tx_aggr.aggr_list (aggr_len, aggr_num updated) and, unless the aggregate is being flushed, the hold timer is armed or its timeout extended. Flushing: mwifiex_usb_prepare_tx_aggr_skb stops the timer, builds one aggregate skb from the list, completing each queued skb; if that allocation fails it completes all queued skbs with -1 and resets aggr_num and aggr_len (its -EBUSY result is not returned by this function); on success the aggregate is sent with mwifiex_usb_construct_send_urb, and if that returns -1 the aggregate is completed with error -1 (the return value is otherwise ignored). Sending the current packet alone: if an aggregate was just sent and the pending data-URB count has reached MWIFIEX_TX_DATA_URB it sets port->block_status, recomputes adapter->data_sent and instead postcopies the packet; otherwise it writes the interface header and returns directly the result of mwifiex_usb_construct_send_urb, which is -EINPROGRESS on submission, -ENOSR if the pending count reached the maximum, or -1 if usb_submit_urb failed (in which case the URB counters and tx_data_ix are rolled back). Postcopy: the packet is appended to the aggregation list and the hold timer is started if not set. In all other cases the function returns -EINPROGRESS.
note: [rev:mixed] r15 (aggregation alloc failure returns -EBUSY / completes the current skb) wrong: -EBUSY comes from the helper at usb.c:896 and is dropped (1067-1075), and only already-queued skbs are completed; r15 (usb_submit_urb failure returns -EINPROGRESS, not -1) right for the aggregate path (the result is ignored, 1070-1074) but the direct-send path returns -1 (1100, 860); r1 (several decision flags can be set together, e.g. send_aggr and postcopy) right; slice cut head, real body 951-1121

name: mt7603_mac_fill_rx
prose: Parses the RX descriptor of a received frame for the mt7603 driver into the mt76_rx_status stored in skb->cb (mt7603/mac.c:504-684; the slice cut the head). It zeroes the status, then reads descriptor words 0, 1 and 2 unconditionally and fills wcid, band, frequency (when the channel index is within the band's channel count), FCS error, MIC error, ICV-error (monitor only) and decrypted/IV-stripped flags. It returns -EINVAL for a max-length error or when the band has no channel table. It then walks the optional descriptor groups, returning -EINVAL whenever, after advancing, the descriptor pointer is at or beyond skb->len: group 4 (skips 4 words), group 1 (IV bytes copied for decrypted CCMP/TKIP/GCMP frames; may request CCMP header insertion), group 2 (timestamp, A-MPDU reference handling), and group 3 (it reads words 0 and 3 of the group before the bounds check; maps the PHY mode: CCK/OFDM rate lookup, HT MCS above 15 or any other mode returns -EINVAL; short GI, LDPC, STBC, rate index, chains, chain signals, 40 MHz bandwidth). A missing group 3 also returns -EINVAL. On -EINVAL skb->data is not pulled, though the status may be partly filled. Otherwise it pulls the descriptor (plus 2 padding bytes when requested) from the skb, inserts the CCMP header if requested, and returns 0 immediately if there is no wcid or the frame is not QoS data; for QoS data frames it also sets aggr (unicast and not QoS-null), qos_ctl and seqno, and returns 0.
note: [rev:right] r15 (three descriptor words are not sufficient: group 3 reads rxd[3] before its bounds check) right: mt7603/mac.c:618-619, 660-661; slice cut head, real body 504-684

name: mt7615_mcu_set_protection
prose: Sends an HT/ERP protection configuration to the mt7615 MCU (real name mt7615_mcu_set_protection(phy, vif, ht_mode, use_cts_prot), mt7615/mcu.c:2568-2613; the slice shows only the second part). It builds a request with prot_idx 2 and band set to whether phy is not the primary phy of the device. For the HT operation protection mode NONMEMBER or NONHT_MIXED it sets prot_mm, prot_gf and prot_bw40; for 20 MHZ protection it sets prot_bw40; it also sets prot_gf when the NON_GF_STA_PRSNT bit is set. If use_cts_prot is true it sets prot_erp_mask to the bit of the vif's omac index (or HW_BSSID_0 when the index is above HW_BSSID_MAX). It returns the result of mt76_mcu_send_msg(MCU_EXT_CMD(PROTECT_CTRL), &req, sizeof(req), true), i.e. 0 on success or a negative errno from the MCU send. The other protection fields stay false/0.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function mt7615_mcu_set_protection; the old contract 'result == 0 || result < 0' is trivial and was removed

name: mt7915_register_device
prose: Registers an mt7915 device (init.c:1219-1297; the slice cut the head). It initialises work items, lists, the reset wait queue and dump mutex, determines dbdc_support and calls mt7915_alloc_ext_phy; if that returns an error it returns it at once with nothing to undo. It then calls mt7915_init_hardware (error: free_phy2), mt7915_init_wiphy, mt76_register_device (error: stop_hw), mt7915_thermal_init (error: unreg_dev) and, if a second phy exists, mt7915_register_ext_phy (error: unreg_thermal). It queues dev->init_work, sets dev->recovery.hw_init_done = true and calls mt7915_init_debugfs and mt7915_coredump_register; a failure of either goes to unreg_ext_phy and returns that error. The unwinding falls through unreg_ext_phy (unregister the external phy if any), unreg_thermal, unreg_dev (mt76_unregister_device), stop_hw (mt7915_stop_hardware) and free_phy2 (ieee80211_free_hw of the second phy if still present). The unwinding does not cancel the already queued init_work and does not reset recovery.hw_init_done. On success it returns 0.

name: mt7915_mac_sta_event
prose: Handles a station lifecycle event for the mt7915 driver (mt7915/main.c:834-877; the slice cut the head). ASSOC: calls mt7915_mcu_add_sta(CONN_STATE_CONNECT, true) and returns its error if it fails; otherwise writes 0xa0 to bits 7:0 of the WTBL LMAC register for the station (mt76_rmw_field), calls mt7915_mcu_add_rate_ctrl(false) and returns its error if it fails, else sets MT_WCID_TX_INFO_SET in msta->wcid.tx_info, msta->wcid.sta = 1, msta->wcid.sta_disabled = 0 and returns 0. AUTHORIZE: calls mt7915_drop_other_sta (which, for an AP vif, iterates the active interfaces of both radios and runs __mt7915_drop_sta with this station's address, so it can affect other stations' entries) and returns the result of mt7915_mcu_add_sta(CONN_STATE_PORT_SECURE, false); it does not itself set any flag in msta->wcid. DISASSOC: tears down every TWT flow of the station, calls mt7915_mcu_add_sta(CONN_STATE_DISCONNECT, false) ignoring its result, clears MT_WCID_TX_INFO_SET, sets sta_disabled = 1 and sta = 0, and returns 0. Any other event returns 0 with no effect.

name: mt7921_pci_probe
prose: PCI probe of the mt7921 driver (mt7921/pci.c:233-399; the slice cut the head). It returns the error directly, with nothing to release, if pcim_enable_device, pcim_iomap_regions or pci_alloc_irq_vectors(1, 1) fails. It sets the memory-space bit and bus mastering, sets a 32-bit DMA mask (error: err_free_pci_vec), optionally disables ASPM, gets the mac80211 ops (NULL: -ENOMEM via err_free_pci_vec) and allocates the mt76 device (-ENOMEM via err_free_pci_vec). From there it sets drvdata and device fields, initialises MMIO and the IRQ tasklet and makes a devm copy of the bus ops with the mt7921 register accessors (-ENOMEM: err_free_dev). It then calls mt792xe_mcu_fw_pmctrl and __mt792xe_mcu_drv_pmctrl, reads the chip id and revision, calls mt792x_wfsys_reset (each error goes to err_free_dev), masks the interrupts, requests the shared IRQ with devm_request_irq (error: err_free_dev), calls mt7921_dma_init and mt7921_register_device (errors: err_free_irq), enables wakeup if the OF node has 'wakeup-source', and returns 0. The error labels fall through: err_free_irq calls devm_free_irq, err_free_dev calls mt76_free_device, err_free_pci_vec calls pci_free_irq_vectors; the other resources (device enable, BAR mapping, the bus-ops copy) are device-managed. The early returns before the vectors were allocated release nothing explicitly.

name: mt7921s_wfsys_reset
prose: Resets the WiFi subsystem of an mt7921 SDIO device (sdio_mac.c:35-77; the slice cut the head). It returns 0 immediately without touching the hardware if dev->mt76.bus_hung is set. Otherwise it calls mt7921s_mcu_drv_pmctrl, claims the SDIO host, clears WF_WHOLE_PATH_RSTB in MCR_WHCR, sleeps 50 ms, clears WF_SDIO_WF_PATH_RSTB (this bit is cleared and not set again in this function), sleeps 1-2 ms, sets WF_WHOLE_PATH_RSTB again and polls MCR_WHCR for WF_RST_DONE (50 ms interval, 2 s timeout; a timeout is ignored). It releases the SDIO host, clears MT76_STATE_MCU_RUNNING in dev->mphy.state and then calls mt7921s_mcu_drv_pmctrl, clears MT_WIFI_PATCH_DL_STATE in MT_CONN_STATUS, calls mt7921s_mcu_fw_pmctrl and finally mt7921s_mcu_drv_pmctrl again (the results of these power-control calls are ignored). It returns 0 in every case.

name: mt7921s_mac_reset
prose: Performs a MAC reset of an mt7921 SDIO device (sdio_mac.c:147-199; the slice cut the head). It frees pending TX skbs and runs mt7921s_host_reset (its result is ignored). If dev->mt76.bus_hung is then set it returns 0 without doing the rest. Otherwise it schedules all TX queues, disables the tx worker, sets MT76_MCU_RESET, wakes the MCU wait queue, purges the MCU response queue, waits up to 5 s for the SDIO TX queues to drain, disables the txrx, status, net and stat workers, disables the SDIO IRQ once and runs mt7921s_wfsys_reset, then re-enables the four SDIO workers, clears dev->fw_assert and MT76_MCU_RESET and enables the SDIO IRQ. It then calls mt7921_run_firmware, mt7921_mcu_set_eeprom, mt7921_mac_init and __mt7921_start in order, stopping at the first non-zero result; it re-enables the tx worker and returns that result (0 on success). The tx worker is re-enabled on every path that disabled it.

name: mt7925_load_clc
prose: Loads the country-listing (CLC) data from the mt7925 firmware file into dev->phy.clc[] (real name mt7925_load_clc(dev, fw_name), mt7925/mcu.c:732-819; the slice starts at request_firmware). It sets dev->phy.clc_chan_conf = 0xff, and returns 0 without doing anything more if mt7925_disable_clc is set or the device is USB. For MMIO devices it reads the hardware encapsulation type from the EEPROM (an error is returned). It requests the firmware (error returned); an invalid firmware (NULL data or smaller than the trailer) gives -EINVAL. It walks the trailer's regions backward from the trailer, accumulating offsets, and returns -EINVAL if a region extends past the file; the first region that has the NON_DL feature and type FW_TYPE_CLC supplies the CLC base. If none is found it returns 0 without loading. Otherwise it iterates the CLC entries in that region: it stops if an entry's idx is beyond the phy->clc array, skips entries already present (after a chip reset), skips entries whose header encapsulation type (or the BE-control table's type) differs from hw_encap, and copies each remaining entry with devm_kmemdup (failure: -ENOMEM). It releases the firmware on every path after it was obtained and returns 0 on success.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function mt7925_load_clc (the slice is its second half)

name: get_own_mld_idx
prose: Static helper in mt7996/main.c (lines 144-164) that picks a free own-MLD index from a 64-bit occupancy mask (bit set = in use). It has no side effects. With group_mld true it searches bits 0 to 15 for the lowest clear bit; with group_mld false it searches bits 16 to 63 for the lowest clear bit and, only if none is clear there, bits 0 to 15. It returns the zero-based index of the lowest clear bit found in the range it searched, or -EINVAL if no clear bit exists in the searched range(s) (for group_mld true: bits 0-15 all set; for false: all 64 bits set).

name: mt7996_ampdu_action
prose: mac80211 ampdu_action callback of mt7996 (mt7996/main.c:1466-1526; static; the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL, before taking dev->mt76.mutex, if sta->txq[params->tid] is NULL. Otherwise it takes dev->mt76.mutex and switches on params->action: RX_START calls mt76_rx_aggr_start on msta->deflink.wcid and then mt7996_mcu_add_rx_ba(..., true), RX_STOP calls mt76_rx_aggr_stop and mt7996_mcu_add_rx_ba(..., false); TX_OPERATIONAL sets mtxq->aggr = true and send_bar = false and calls mt7996_mcu_add_tx_ba(..., true); TX_STOP_FLUSH and TX_STOP_FLUSH_CONT clear mtxq->aggr and the tid bit of msta->deflink.wcid.ampdu_state and call mt7996_mcu_add_tx_ba(..., false); TX_STOP_CONT does the same and then also calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe(vif, sta->addr, tid) whatever the firmware call returned; TX_START sets the tid bit in ampdu_state and returns IEEE80211_AMPDU_TX_START_IMMEDIATE. The mutex is released and ret returned: the value of the firmware BA call for the cases that make one, IEEE80211_AMPDU_TX_START_IMMEDIATE for TX_START, and 0 for any other action. Within this function ampdu_state is only modified by TX_START and the three TX stop actions; the mt76_rx_aggr_* helpers do not touch it (it is not referenced in agg-rx.c).

name: handle_rcvd_ntwrk_info
prose: Work handler of the wilc1000 driver (hif.c:538-571; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head) that reports a received scan result frame. msg is the host_if_msg containing the work item; msg->body.net_info holds the received management frame (mgmt, frame_len) and the scan request is taken from msg->vif->hif_drv->usr_scan_req. If the frame is a probe response or a beacon it sets the offset of the information elements for that type; any other frame skips the reporting. It takes the IE pointer through the u.beacon.variable member for both frame types (the offsets only coincide because both layouts start with the same fixed fields) and the IE length as frame_len minus the type's offset; a non-positive length skips the reporting. Otherwise it finds the DS-parameter-set IE and, if present with a non-zero length, stores its channel byte in rcvd_info->ch, and, if scan_req->scan_result is non-NULL, calls it with SCAN_EVENT_NETWORK_FOUND, rcvd_info and scan_req->priv. On every path it frees the mgmt buffer and the msg.

name: qtnf_parse_variable_mac_info
prose: Parses the TLV part of a qtnfmac 'get MAC info' response (real name qtnf_parse_variable_mac_info(mac, resp, tlv_buf_size), commands.c:1007-1214; static; the slice starts at its beginning of the regulatory handling). It returns -E2BIG (after WARN_ON) if resp->n_reg_rules exceeds NL80211_MAX_SUPP_REG_RULES, allocates mac->rd for the rules (-ENOMEM on failure; it is not freed on later error returns here), copies the rule count and alpha2 and maps the DFS region. It then walks the TLVs: interface-limit records require an existing interface-combination array (-EINVAL if none), are counted but not stored past macinfo.n_if_comb (a warning), must have a length matching their n_limits (-EINVAL) and are converted into an allocated limits array (-ENOMEM on failure); extended-capability and mask TLVs must be at most 255 bytes (-EINVAL) and are remembered by pointer; WoWLAN capability TLVs shorter than the header or with a mismatched length return -EINVAL, an empty one is skipped, and otherwise the old WoWLAN info is freed and re-parsed; regulatory-rule TLVs return -EINVAL if there are more than resp->n_reg_rules, if the length is wrong, and otherwise fill mac->rd->reg_rules[rule_idx++]; unknown TLV types only log. After the walk it returns -EINVAL if the TLV buffer was malformed, if the parsed combination count differs from macinfo.n_if_comb, if the ext-capability and mask lengths differ, or if rule_idx differs from n_reg_rules. If extended capabilities are present it duplicates them and the mask (-ENOMEM on failure, freeing the first copy), frees the previous ones with qtnf_mac_ext_caps_free and stores the new copies in macinfo; it returns 0 on success.

name: rt2x00lib_antenna_diversity_sample
prose: Evaluates the RSSI samples gathered while sampling antennas (rt2x00link.c:67-106; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It takes sample_current = the averaged RSSI of the antenna in use if the link has received frames (link.qual.rx_success non-zero), otherwise DEFAULT_RSSI, and sample_other = link.ant.rssi_history if it is non-zero, otherwise DEFAULT_RSSI. It copies the active antenna setup, clears ANTENNA_MODE_SAMPLE in link.ant.flags and, if sample_current >= sample_other, stores sample_current in rssi_history and returns without changing the antenna configuration. Otherwise it leaves rssi_history unchanged, picks the antenna opposite to the active RX antenna (ANTENNA_B if active.rx is ANTENNA_A, else ANTENNA_A), sets new_ant.rx to it when ANTENNA_RX_DIVERSITY is set and new_ant.tx to the same antenna (derived from active.rx) when ANTENNA_TX_DIVERSITY is set, and calls rt2x00lib_config_antenna with the new setup.

name: rt73usb_config_shared_key
prose: Configures a shared (group) key in an RT73 USB device (rt73usb.c:256-351; static; the slice cut the head). For SET_KEY it computes mask = 0xf << crypto->bssidx, reads SEC_CSR0 and keeps only the masked bits, and returns -ENOSPC (no register written, key unchanged) if that value is non-zero and equal to the whole mask. Otherwise it adds to key->hw_key_idx the value ffz() of the masked value (0 if the masked value is 0), which is the index of the lowest zero bit of the masked value and so may lie outside the BSS's four-bit window when bssidx is not 0. It writes the key and the TX/RX MIC from crypto to SHARED_KEY_ENTRY(key->hw_key_idx), stores the cipher in a 3-bit field of SEC_CSR1 if hw_key_idx < 8 or of SEC_CSR5 otherwise, and sets IEEE80211_KEY_FLAG_GENERATE_IV in key->flags. For both SET_KEY and DISABLE_KEY (and for any other command) it then reads SEC_CSR0, sets bit (1 << key->hw_key_idx) for SET_KEY or clears it for DISABLE_KEY, writes SEC_CSR0 back and returns 0. The shifts are only well defined if the resulting hw_key_idx is within the register widths (callers must keep it in range).
note: [rev:n/a] fixed-unreviewed; read rt73usb.c:256-351; the earlier reviewer notes about ffz outside the BSS mask and out-of-range indices were right and are now stated

name: rt73usb_config_pairwise_key
prose: Configures a pairwise key in an RT73 USB device (rt73usb.c:353-455; static; the slice cut the head). For SET_KEY it reads SEC_CSR2; if it is non-zero and all ones it sets key->hw_key_idx to 32 and reads SEC_CSR3; if that is also non-zero and all ones it returns -ENOSPC (key->hw_key_idx has by then been set to 32, nothing is written to the hardware and key->flags is unchanged). It adds ffz() of the register value read last (SEC_CSR2 when it was not full, else SEC_CSR3; 0 if that value is 0) to key->hw_key_idx (when SEC_CSR2 was not full the old index is used as the base and SEC_CSR3 is not examined). It writes the key and MICs to PAIRWISE_KEY_ENTRY(hw_key_idx), the peer address and cipher to PAIRWISE_TA_ENTRY(hw_key_idx), sets bit (1 << crypto->bssidx) in SEC_CSR4 and sets IEEE80211_KEY_FLAG_GENERATE_IV. For every command it then updates the valid bit for hw_key_idx in SEC_CSR2 (hw_key_idx < 32) or SEC_CSR3 (bit hw_key_idx - 32): set for SET_KEY, cleared for DISABLE_KEY, unchanged for any other value, writes the register back and returns 0. The shifts are only well defined for hw_key_idx within the register widths.
note: [rev:n/a] fixed-unreviewed; read rt73usb.c:353-455; earlier reviewer notes (SEC_CSR3 not checked when SEC_CSR2 not full; out-of-range final index) right and now stated

name: rtl8180_detect_rf
prose: Detects which RTL8225 RF variant an rtl8180 device has (real name rtl8180_detect_rf(dev), rtl818x/rtl8180/rtl8225.c:744-767; the slice shows only its end). It writes RFPinsOutput (0x0480), RFPinsSelect (0x0488) and RFPinsEnable (0x1FFF), reads EEPROM_CMD, sleeps 100 ms, writes 0x1B7 to RF register 0, reads RF registers 8 and 9, writes 0x0B7 to RF register 0 (restoring it), and returns a pointer to rtl8225_ops if register 8 is not 0x588 or register 9 is not 0x700, otherwise a pointer to rtl8225z2_ops. It returns no error values.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; the slice is the tail of rtl8180_detect_rf (hw rtl8180 variant, not rtl8187 as the old prose said)

name: btc8723b2ant_is_common_action
prose: Applies the 'common' Bluetooth-coexistence action of the RTL8723B 2-antenna manager when a simple case matches and reports whether it did (halbtc8723b2ant.c:1669-1777; static; the slice cut the head). It reads the BT HS operation, WiFi connected and WiFi busy states. If WiFi is not connected it sets low-power-disable false, applies limited-RX, writes RF register 0x1, sets coex table type 0, turns TDMA off, sets the firmware DAC swing level to 6, sets decrease-BT-power 0 and the software mechanism (all off), and returns true. If WiFi is connected and coex_dm->bt_status is NON_CONNECTED_IDLE it does the same with DAC swing 0xb and returns true. If bt_status is CONNECTED_IDLE it sets low-power-disable true and returns false at once when BT HS is on; otherwise it applies limited-RX, RF register, coex table 0, TDMA off, DAC swing 0xb, decrease-BT-power 0 and the software mechanism with its first flag set, and returns true. For any other bt_status (BT busy) it sets low-power-disable true and returns false if WiFi is busy, otherwise it returns the result of btc8723b2ant_action_wifi_idle_process (whose settings it applies). The low-power-disable setting is sent with the btc_set callback in each branch.

name: btc8821a1ant_set_ant_path
prose: Programs the antenna path registers of the RTL8821A 1-antenna coexistence manager (halbtc8821a1ant.c:918-1000; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). The three branches differ. init_hw_cfg true: it reads register 0x4c, clears bit 23, sets bit 24 and writes it back, writes 0x3 to the bits of register 0x975 selected by mask 0x3, writes 0xcb4 = 0x77, and sends H2C command 0x65 with two bytes: {1, 1} if board_info->btdm_ant_pos is BTC_ANTENNA_AT_MAIN_PORT, else {0, 1}. wifi_off true (and init_hw_cfg false): it reads register 0x4c, clears bits 23 and 24 and writes it back, and writes 0x3 to the bits of register 0x765 selected by mask 0x18; 0x975 is not touched. Otherwise (both false): it writes 0x0 to the 0x765 bits selected by mask 0x18; 0x4c and 0x975 are not touched. After that, in every case, it writes 0xcb4 and the bits of register 0xcb7 selected by mask 0x30 according to ant_pos_type: BTC_ANT_PATH_WIFI writes 0xcb4 = 0x77 and 0xcb7 field = 1 for the main-port antenna position, else 2; BTC_ANT_PATH_BT writes 0xcb4 = 0x77 and the field = 2 for the main port, else 1; BTC_ANT_PATH_PTA or any other value writes 0xcb4 = 0x66 and the field = 1 for the main port, else 2 (so in the init branch the 0xcb4 value 0x77 may be overwritten by 0x66).

name: rtl_op_bss_info_changed
prose: mac80211 bss_info_changed callback of rtlwifi (real name rtl_op_bss_info_changed, core.c:1008-1324; static, returns nothing). It takes rtlpriv->locks.conf_mutex and releases it at the out label on every path. For ad-hoc, AP and mesh vifs it enables beaconing (updates the interrupt mask, linked_set_reg, sends a beacon) when BSS_CHANGED_BEACON or BEACON_ENABLED with enable_beacon is set and it was off, disables it for BEACON_ENABLED without enable_beacon, and applies the beacon interval for BEACON_INT. For BSS_CHANGED_ASSOC with vif->cfg.assoc it resets the security info and CAM, sets link_state, assoc_id and bssid, calls linked_set_reg, then under rcu_read_lock looks the BSS up with ieee80211_find_sta: if the station is not found it leaves the RCU section and jumps to out, skipping all later flags; otherwise it may send an SMPS action, derives mac->mode (A, B, G, N, AC) from band and station capabilities, updates the rate table for station vifs, leaves the RCU section and sets the keep-alive register. For disassociation it leaves LPS and P2P PS, clears link_state, unlinks the BSS from cfg80211, zeroes the bssid and mode. Either way it then sets the network type, reports the join status to the firmware and BT-coex. It then handles ERP_CTS_PROT (use_cts_protect), ERP_PREAMBLE, ERP_SLOT (slot time register) and HT (under RCU, raises the A-MPDU density and lowers the factor from the peer, and writes the HT registers). For BSS_CHANGED_BSSID it writes the BSSID register, records the bssid, looks up the station under RCU (not found: leave RCU and jump to out), recomputes mac->mode and the vendor/ht/vht flags and, for station vifs, the station's wireless_mode, and, if BSS_CHANGED_BASIC_RATES is also set, the basic rate set and register; it leaves the RCU section before reaching out. Flags after a failed station lookup are not processed.

name: _rtl88e_fill_h2c_command
prose: Writes one host-to-firmware (H2C) command into a hardware message box of an RTL8188EE (rtl8188ee/fw.c:165-333; static; the slice cut the head). It first waits for any other H2C write in progress, polling in 100 microsecond steps with the lock dropped; if the wait counter exceeds 1000 it returns at once without writing anything (the other caller's rtlhal->h2c_setinprogress stays set). Otherwise it sets h2c_setinprogress under rtlpriv->locks.h2c_lock and releases the lock. It selects the box from rtlhal->last_hmeboxnum (0-3), checks whether the firmware has read the previous command and, if not, polls up to about 100 times at 10 microseconds; if the box is still not free it logs a debug message and writes nothing (last_hmeboxnum unchanged). Otherwise it builds the box content with element_id in byte 0: for cmd_len 1-3 it copies cmd_len bytes after it and writes 4 bytes to the box register; for cmd_len 4-7 it copies the first 3 payload bytes into the box content and bytes from index 3 into a 4-byte extension buffer, then writes 2 bytes to the extension register and 4 bytes to the box register, so for cmd_len 6 or 7 the payload bytes beyond the first five are not written to the hardware; for any other cmd_len it only logs an error. In all of these written/unsupported cases it marks the write done and advances last_hmeboxnum modulo 4 (this also happens for an unsupported cmd_len). Finally it clears h2c_setinprogress under the lock and returns. cmd_b must be readable for cmd_len bytes when cmd_len is 1 to 7 (it is not read otherwise).

name: rtl92c_bt_state_change
prose: Detects a Bluetooth state change for the rtl8192c coexistence logic and updates the related registers (dm_common.c:1497-1579; static; the slice cut the head). It returns false with no change if mac80211.link_state is below MAC80211_LINKED. It reads register 0x4fd, the masked counters at 0x488 and 0x48c and the polling count at 0x490; if the counters and 0x4fd all read the 'inactive' pattern (BT_MASK, BT_MASK, 0xffffffff, 0xff) it returns false. It takes bit 0 of 0x4fd as the BT state. If it differs from btcoexist.bt_cur_state it stores it and, only when btcoexist.reg_bt_sco == 3, sets bt_service to BT_IDLE and writes 0x4fd with that bit OR (BIT(1) unless bt_ant_isolation == 1) OR BIT(2); it returns true in either case (the ratios are not updated in this case). Otherwise it computes ratio_tx = bt_tx * 1000 / polling and ratio_pri = bt_pri * 1000 / polling (polling must be non-zero here), stores them in btcoexist.ratio_tx and ratio_pri, and, only when the BT state bit is set and reg_bt_sco == 3, classifies the service (IDLE, SCO, BUSY, OTHERBUSY, PAN or OTHER_ACTION from the ratios); if the service type differs from bt_service it stores it, writes interrupt-migration registers 0x504/0x506/0x507 (0x0ccc, 0x54, 0x54 for non-idle, or 0x00 in 0x506 and 0x507 for idle), writes 0x4fd with the state bit plus BIT(1) (unless bt_ant_isolation == 1) and BIT(2) (only for idle), and returns true. In all other cases it returns false.

name: rtl92cu_gpio_radio_on_off_checking
prose: Polls the hardware radio-kill input of an RTL8192CU device and applies a change (real name rtl92cu_gpio_radio_on_off_checking(hw, valid), rtl8192cu/hw.c:2067-2171; the slice shows only its tail). It returns false, without setting *valid, if ppsc->swrf_processing is set or another RF change is in progress (rfchange_inprogress, checked and set under rf_ps_lock). Otherwise it reads the requested state: in power-down mode from bit 7 of REG_HSISR (set = RF off), else after clearing bit 3 of REG_MAC_PINMUX_CFG from bit 3 of REG_GPIO_IO_SEL (set = RF on). If the radio is marked off and the request is on, or it is marked on and the request is off, it flips ppsc->hwradiooff and records that a change is applied; then, in that case, it sets hwradiooff to true again, clears the ASPM or D3 power-save level when turning on, clears rfchange_inprogress under the lock, writes REG_RSV_CTRL and REG_APS_FSMCO in power-down mode when turning off, and sets the ASPM or D3 power-save level when turning off. If nothing changed but the request is off or the current state is off, it sets the power-save level and clears rfchange_inprogress; otherwise it only clears rfchange_inprogress. It then sets *valid = 1 and returns !ppsc->hwradiooff.

name: _rtl92ee_init_mac
prose: Initialises the MAC of an RTL8192EE (real name _rtl92ee_init_mac(hw), rtl8192ee/hw.c:730-927; static; the slice is its middle and end). It tunes the crystal/AFE registers, then runs the power-on sequence (rtl_hal_pwrseqcmdparsing with RTL8192E_NIC_ENABLE_FLOW) and returns false if it fails. It writes control and clock registers (CR, HWSEQ_CTRL, SYS_CLKR, GPIO_MUXCFG) and, when rtlhal->mac_func_enable is not set, initialises the LLT table, returning false if that fails. It clears interrupt status, sets the TRX DMA control, programs the TX/RX descriptor ring base addresses (upper 32 bits only when the dma64 module parameter is set), the queue and beacon-related registers, SIFS/NAV/ACK-timeout values, aggregation limits and the multicast address filter, refreshes the LED state, and returns true. The visible failure returns are the power-sequence and LLT ones, both false.

name: _rtl92se_macconfig_before_fwdownload
prose: Programs the RTL8192SE MAC before the firmware is downloaded (rtl8192se/hw.c:528-741; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). If rtlpci->first_init is set it resets the PCIe digital block via REG_SYS_FUNC_EN. It switches to SW IO control: if bit 7 of SYS_CLKR+1 is set it calls _rtl92se_halset_sysclk and returns immediately, leaving everything else undone, if that call fails. It then programs the AFE PLL, LDO, clocks and isolation registers, resets the MAC-IO and core digital blocks, and calls _rtl92se_halset_sysclk again, returning immediately if that fails. It writes CMDR and a set of fixed MAC register values, the initial MCS selects, and the DMA descriptor base addresses of the RX MPDU and command rings and of the TX rings, then writes CMDR 0x37FC and polls TCR (up to 21 reads, 5 us apart) until TXDMA_INIT_VALUE is seen. The following 'timeout' check tests pollingcnt <= 0 on a u8 that is post-decremented, so after a real timeout pollingcnt has wrapped to 255 and the error log and the TXDMA_EN toggle in CMDR are not executed; they run only if the poll succeeds on the last (21st) read with the counter at 0. Finally, if ppsc->rfoff_reason is RF_CHANGE_BY_IPS or 0 and _rtl92se_rf_onoff_detect reports ERFON, it turns the software LED on.

name: _rtl92s_phy_set_fwcmd_io
prose: Sends the pending firmware command held in rtlhal->current_fwcmd_io to an RTL8192SE (rtl8192se/phy.c:1183-1319; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). If is_hal_stop(rtlhal) it returns immediately without touching registers or fields (rtlhal->set_fwcmd_inprogress is not cleared on this path). If the firmware version is at least 0x34 it first remaps FW_CMD_RA_REFRESH_N and FW_CMD_RA_REFRESH_BG in rtlhal->current_fwcmd_io to the _COMB variants. It then dispatches: FW_CMD_RA_RESET, RA_ACTIVE, RA_REFRESH_N_COMB, RA_REFRESH_BG_COMB, IQK_ENABLE, LPS_LEAVE, ADD_A2_ENTRY and CTRL_DM_BY_DRIVER write their command word to WFM5 and call rtl92s_phy_chk_fwcmd_iodone; RA_REFRESH_N and RA_REFRESH_BG (only reachable on firmware older than 0x34) do two write-and-check cycles (FW_RA_REFRESH, then FW_RA_ENABLE_RSSI_MASK or FW_RA_DISABLE_RSSI_MASK); LPS_ENTER writes FW_LPS_ENTER ORed with ((assoc_id | 0xc000) << 8) and checks; PAUSE_DM_BY_SCAN lowers the initial gain (0x17 in the AGC core registers of paths A and B) and sets the CCA threshold to 0x40; RESUME_DM_BY_SCAN restores the CCA threshold to 0xcd and re-sets the TX power; HIGH_PWR_DISABLE does nothing if HAL_DM_HIPWR_DISABLE is set in dm_flag, else lowers the initial gain and sets the CCA threshold like the pause case; HIGH_PWR_ENABLE does nothing if HAL_DM_HIPWR_DISABLE is set or dynamic TX power is enabled, else restores the CCA threshold to 0xcd; any other value does nothing. After the switch it calls rtl92s_phy_chk_fwcmd_iodone once more (for every non-stopped case) and clears rtlhal->set_fwcmd_inprogress.

name: rtl92s_phy_set_fw_cmd
prose: Issues a firmware command on an RTL8192SE (rtl8192se/phy.c:1321-1545; the slice cut the head). It reads the current command map and parameter registers and decides, per command, whether the command is handled by writing the map/parameter registers inline or needs post-processing through _rtl92s_phy_set_fwcmd_io. With firmware version >= 0x35 it remaps FW_CMD_RA_REFRESH_N/BG to the _COMB variants; with an older firmware, FW_CMD_IQK_ENABLE, RA_REFRESH_N and RA_REFRESH_BG set postprocessing and no register is written inline. With version >= 0x3E FW_CMD_CTRL_DM_BY_DRIVER becomes FW_CMD_CTRL_DM_BY_DRIVER_NEW. Inline commands (RA_INIT, DIG_DISABLE, DIG_ENABLE/RESUME [only if DIG is not disabled in dm_flag], DIG_HALT, TXPWR_TRACK_THERMAL, RA_REFRESH_N_COMB, RA_REFRESH_BG_COMB, IQK_ENABLE, CTRL_DM_BY_DRIVER_NEW, DIG_MODE_FA/SS, PAPE_CONTROL) update the command map register (and, for TXPWR_TRACK_THERMAL and the RA _COMB commands, the parameter register), often clearing the control bit afterwards. RESUME_DM_BY_SCAN, PAUSE_DM_BY_SCAN and HIGH_PWR_DISABLE update the map register and set postprocessing; HIGH_PWR_ENABLE does so only when HAL_DM_HIPWR_DISABLE is not set and dynamic TX power is off; any command without a case (the default case) sets postprocessing without any inline write. At the end, if postprocessing is set and rtlhal->set_fwcmd_inprogress is false, it sets set_fwcmd_inprogress, stores the (possibly remapped) command in rtlhal->current_fwcmd_io, calls _rtl92s_phy_set_fwcmd_io and returns true. Otherwise (no postprocessing, or a command already in progress) it returns false and leaves set_fwcmd_inprogress unchanged; inline commands that did their register writes still return false.

name: rtl8723be_dm_txpower_tracking_callback_thermalmeter
prose: Thermal-meter based TX power tracking for the RTL8723BE (rtl8723be/dm.c:722-878; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It sets rtlpriv->dm.txpower_trackinginit = true, reads the RF thermal meter, and returns immediately, without touching txpowercount or anything else, if txpower_track_control is clear, the reading is 0 or eeprom_thermalmeter is 0xFF. Otherwise, if rtldm->thermalvalue is 0 it sets thermalvalue_lck and thermalvalue_iqk to the raw reading; it stores the reading in the thermalvalue_avg ring (advancing and wrapping thermalvalue_avg_index at AVG_THERMAL_NUM_8723BE) and replaces the reading by the average of the non-zero ring entries. It computes the absolute differences delta (to rtldm->thermalvalue), delta_lck and delta_iqk; if delta_lck >= IQK_THRESHOLD it records the averaged value as thermalvalue_lck and runs rtl8723be_phy_lc_calibrate. If delta > 0 and txpower_track_control is set it recomputes delta as the difference to eeprom_thermalmeter (capped at TXSCALE_TABLE_SIZE - 1), picks delta_power_index[A] from the up or down swing table (saving the previous value in delta_power_index_last), sets power_index_offset[A] to 0 if unchanged or to the difference, computes ofdm_index[0] and cck_index from the base swing indexes plus the offset, copies the unclamped values to swing_idx_ofdm[0] and swing_idx_cck, and then clamps ofdm_index[0] to [ofdm_min_index (6), OFDM_TABLE_SIZE-1] and cck_index to [0, CCK_TABLE_SIZE-1]; otherwise it sets power_index_offset[A] to 0. If power_index_offset[A] is non-zero and tracking is enabled it sets done_txpower, calls rtl8723be_dm_tx_power_track_set_power, copies the swing indexes into the base values and stores the thermal value in rtldm->thermalvalue. If delta_iqk >= IQK_THRESHOLD it records the value as thermalvalue_iqk and runs rtl8723be_phy_iq_calibrate(hw, false). It finally sets rtldm->txpowercount to 0.

name: _rtl8723be_fill_h2c_command
prose: Writes one host-to-firmware (H2C) command into a hardware message box of an RTL8723BE (rtl8723be/fw.c:26-195; static; the slice cut the head). It first waits for any other H2C write in progress, polling in 100 microsecond steps with h2c_lock released between polls; if the counter exceeds 1000 it returns at once without writing and without touching h2c_setinprogress (left set by the other writer). Otherwise it sets h2c_setinprogress under h2c_lock. The following loop body executes only once in practice, since every pass either breaks or marks the write done, so its 100-attempt limit is never reached. It selects the box from rtlhal->last_hmeboxnum (0-3) and waits (about 100 polls, 10 microseconds apart) for the firmware to have read the previous command; if it did not, it logs a debug message and writes nothing (last_hmeboxnum unchanged). Otherwise it builds the box content with element_id in byte 0 and writes: for cmd_len 1-3, cmd_len bytes of p_cmdbuffer after it into the four box registers; for cmd_len 4-7, the first 3 bytes into the box and bytes 3 to cmd_len-1 into the four extension registers (extension written first). For any other cmd_len it only logs an error. After the write (and also for an unsupported cmd_len) it advances last_hmeboxnum modulo 4. It then clears h2c_setinprogress under the lock and returns. p_cmdbuffer must be readable for cmd_len bytes when cmd_len is 1 to 7.

name: _rtl8723be_reset_pcie_interface_dma
prose: Resets the PCIe DMA interface of an RTL8723BE (rtl8723be/hw.c:1215-1323; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It clears bits 1:0 of REG_RSV_CTRL and sets bit 2 of REG_PMC_DBG_CTRL2 (unlocking the registers). It pauses RX DMA by setting bit 2 of REG_RXDMA_CONTROL unless it was already set, remembering whether it did, saves REG_PCIE_CTRL_REG+1 and writes 0xFF to it if it was not already 0xFF. If mac_power_on is true it writes 0 to REG_CR. It then clears and afterwards sets bit 0 of REG_SYS_FUNC_EN+1 (PCIe DMA reset and enable), and, if mac_power_on, writes 0xFF to REG_CR. It always sets bit 1 of REG_MAC_PHY_CTRL_NORMAL+2. Only when mac_power_on is false does it release RX DMA (clearing bit 2 of REG_RXDMA_CONTROL if it had set it) and restore the saved REG_PCIE_CTRL_REG+1 value; when mac_power_on is true the RX pause bit and the 0xFF pause value stay in place (released later by the caller). Finally it clears bit 2 of REG_PMC_DBG_CTRL2 to lock the registers.

name: _rtl8723be_phy_path_b_iqk
prose: Runs the path-B TX IQ calibration of an RTL8723BE and returns a status byte (rtl8723be/phy.c:1671-1741; static; the slice cut the head). It leaves IQK mode, switches to path B, sets the RF registers 0xed and 0x43 of path A, programs the IQK, tone, PI and LO calibration registers, enters IQK mode, triggers the one-shot LOK/IQK with two writes to RIQK_AGC_PTS, waits mdelay(IQK_DELAY_TIME) and leaves IQK mode. It then reads RRX_POWER_AFTER_IQK_A_2, RTX_POWER_BEFORE_IQK_A and RTX_POWER_AFTER_IQK_A. It returns 0x00 unless bit 28 of the first value is clear and the 10-bit fields (bits 16-25) of the second and third are not 0x142 and 0x42; in that case it sets bit 0 of the result, and then returns 0x01 (the second check, on the transformed third value and the range 0xf0 to 0x110 of the second, also leads to a result of 0x01 or, if it fails, returns the value already set, which is 0x01). The only values this function returns are 0x00 and 0x01; bit 1 is not set here.

name: rtl8821ae_set_hw_reg
prose: Sets one hardware variable of an RTL8821AE/8812AE (rtl8821ae/hw.c:470-784; returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It switches on variable, reading the value from val according to the selector and either writing registers or updating driver state: ETHER_ADDR and BSSID write six bytes of val to REG_MACID/REG_BSSID; BASIC_RATE writes the 16-bit value masked with 0x15f to REG_RRSR; SIFS, R2T_SIFS, SLOT_TIME (which also re-applies HW_VAR_AC_PARAM for each AC), ACK_PREAMBLE, WPA_CONFIG, SHORTGI_DENSITY (ORs the density into mac->min_space_cfg without clearing the old bits), AMPDU_FACTOR (hardware-type dependent length), AC_PARAM and ACM_CTRL, RCR (also stored in rtlpci->receive_config), RETRY_LIMIT, DUAL_TSF_RST, SET_RPWM and CORRECT_TSF write registers; AMPDU_MIN_SPACE does nothing unless the value is at most 7 (and stores that value back into *val); NAV_UPPER does nothing but log if the value exceeds HAL_92C_NAV_UPPER_UNIT * 0xFF; EFUSE_BYTES, EFUSE_USAGE and FW_PSMODE_STATUS update driver fields; IO_CMD, H2C_FW_PWRMODE, RESUME_CLK_ON, FW_LPS_ACTION, H2C_FW_P2P_PS_OFFLOAD, KEEP_ALIVE and H2C_FW_JOINBSSRPT call firmware helpers (JOINBSSRPT with RT_MEDIA_CONNECT first re-sets HW_VAR_AID with val NULL and downloads the reserved page); AID reads and writes REG_BCN_PSR_RPT using mac->assoc_id and does not use val; INIT_RTS_RATE does nothing; an unknown variable is only logged. val must point to a value of the type the selector expects (a u8, u16, u32, bool or ETH_ALEN bytes), except for HW_VAR_AID where it may be NULL.
note: [rev:right] r15 (HW_VAR_AID is called internally with NULL, but the precondition required val to point to a buffer) right: hw.c:723-724, 733-739; real function rtl8821ae_set_hw_reg at 470-784 (slice cut head)

name: rtl8821ae_sw_led_on
prose: Turns a software LED on for the RTL8821AE (rtl8821ae/led.c:9-35; the slice cut the head; returns nothing). It first logs the LED address and pin for every call. For LED_PIN_LED0 it reads REG_LEDCFG2, clears bit 6 and writes back (value & 0xf0) | BIT(5). For LED_PIN_LED1 it reads REG_LEDCFG1 and writes back value & 0x10 (all other bits cleared). For LED_PIN_GPIO0 it does nothing further (no register access). For any other pin it logs 'switch case not processed' and writes no register.
note: [rev:mixed] r15 (GPIO0 writes no register and does not log in the case) right about the case itself (led.c:18-19), but the function logs once for every pin at 14-15; r1 (LED1 path writes value & 0x10, clearing bits) right: 26-29

name: calculate_bit_shift
prose: Static inline helper in rtlwifi wifi.h (lines 3031-3037) that returns the shift of the lowest set bit of a register bitmask. If bitmask is 0 it issues WARN_ON_ONCE (a warning only the first time) and returns 0. Otherwise it returns __ffs(bitmask), the zero-based index (0 to 31) of the least significant set bit, so bit number result of bitmask is set and all lower bits are clear. It has no side effects other than the warning.
note: [rev:right] earlier random-testing rejections of the contract (result 17 for 65536) disagree with __ffs (which gives 16, zero-based), likely a test-harness definition of __ffs; contract field left empty; wifi.h:3031-3037

name: rtw_load_rfk_table
prose: Loads the RF calibration init table of an rtw88 chip (real name rtw_load_rfk_table(rtwdev), rtw88/phy.c:1831-1848; static; returns nothing). If chip->rfk_init_tbl is NULL it returns at once with no effect. Otherwise it sets bit 17 of register 0x1e24, sets bits 28, 29 and 30 and clears bit 31 of register 0x1cd0, loads chip->rfk_init_tbl with rtw_load_table, and sets rtwdev->dm_info.dpk_info.is_dpk_pwr_on to true. No lock is taken.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function rtw_load_rfk_table (the listed name rtw_phy_load_rfk_table does not exist)

name: _update_bt_info
prose: Parses a Bluetooth info report received by the rtw89 coexistence code and updates the BT state (real name _update_bt_info(rtwdev, buf, len), rtw89/coex.c:8030-8163; static, returns nothing; the slice shows only its middle). It returns without any change if buf[BTC_BTINFO_L1] is not 6, and, counting it in cnt_bt[BTC_BCNT_INFOSAME], if the report is identical to the stored bt->raw_info. Otherwise it copies the report to bt->raw_info and parses it byte by byte: low byte 2 (connect, SCO/ACL busy, inquiry/page state and its counter, profile existence flags for HFP, HID, A2DP and PAN and the profile count, trx_info.bt_profile), low byte 3 (retry and inquiry/page counters, cqddr, mesh busy), high byte 0 (BT RSSI through chip->ops->btc_get_bt_rssi and the RSSI level), high byte 1 (BLE connection and HID type, re-init, re-link, ignore-WLAN and role-switch edge counters; when ignore-WLAN is set and the WLAN RF is not off it calls _set_bt_ignore_wlan_act(rtwdev, false)), high byte 2 (PAN/A2DP activity, AFH update counter, slave role, HID slot info and pair count, HID type bits), and high byte 3 (A2DP bitpool, 3M rate-change counter, sink flag; on A2DP appearing it resets vendor id, flush time and play latency and queues the BT device-info work). Finally it calls _run_coex(rtwdev, BTC_RSN_UPDATE_BT_INFO). len is not used.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; the slice is the middle of _update_bt_info (coex.c:8030-8163), whole function read

name: rtw89_load_rfe_data_from_fw
prose: Builds the RFE TX-power parameter set from firmware-loaded configuration (real name rtw89_load_rfe_data_from_fw(rtwdev, init), rtw89/fw.c:10094-10188; the slice shows only its end). If rtwdev->rfe_data is NULL it returns init unchanged. Otherwise it uses &rfe_data->rfe_parms as parms, starting from a copy of *init when init is non-NULL. For each of the by-rate table, the 2/5/6 GHz limit tables (regular and DA), the RU limit tables (regular and DA) and the TX shape limit tables, if the corresponding firmware configuration is valid (rtw89_txpwr_conf_valid) it loads the table (or sets the by-rate loader) and points the matching parms field at it; invalid ones leave the field as copied from init. It then sets parms->has_da with rtw89_fw_has_da_txpwr_table(rtwdev, parms) and returns parms.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; the slice is the tail of rtw89_load_rfe_data_from_fw; start of the function (10094-10170) read
